critical_code_review_comments: content.js uses a module-level `cache` with no exported way to force-refresh from outside ContentPage. If any non-admin UI mutates content, the home useContent() will keep stale data until a hard refresh. Low priority — admin ContentPage already calls refetchContent() on save.

In headless Chromium, /api/media mp4 fails H.264 decode and the browser falls back to /hero.webm. In production browsers the user's uploaded mp4 will decode natively — behaviour verified by readyState progression and currentTime advancing in test.

context_for_next_testing_agent: The <video key={hero.video_url}> fix in Hero.jsx is working as intended: when useContent transitions from DEFAULT_CONTENT (/hero.mp4) to real content (/api/media/<id>), the key change forces React to unmount+remount the <video>, re-evaluating <source> children per HTML spec. Verified without page reload via window.__marker init-script survival. All 5 user media docs remain intact; current server state video_media_id=6abed24ce3c1d38a2ac02221.
rca of the issue: ROOT CAUSE (confirmed by main agent, now verified by this test): HTML <video> element only reads its <source> children once at mount per the spec. Previous Hero.jsx mounted with DEFAULT_CONTENT (/hero.mp4) during the ~200-500ms /api/content in-flight window, then when useContent() returned real content the React re-render only updated the <source src=...> attribute but the already-mounted <video> ignored it. FIX: `key={hero.video_url}` on <video> forces React to unmount+remount whenever video_url changes, which causes a fresh <source> enumeration and the correct uploaded video to load. VERIFICATION: source[0] attribute now points to /api/media/6abed24ce3c1d38a2ac02221, video.paused=false, currentTime advances; no reload (init-script marker preserved).
